exposure: Maternal age (adolescents, late adolescents, young women)
Maternal age (adolescents ≤19 years, late adolescents 20-24 years, and young women 25-30 years)
outcome: Pelvic Organ Prolapse Distress Inventory (POPDI) scores
cohort: 285 women up to 30 years old, 6 months postpartum, living in the urban area of Western Amazon in the city of Rio Branco, Acre, Brazil
finding: Adolescents had a higher prevalence of PFD and more severe symptoms compared to young women, and cesarean delivery was associated with a greater negative impact on pelvic floor health in adolescents.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a higher prevalence of UI, UUI, and FI, as well as higher POPDI, UDI, and PFDI scores in adolescents compared to young women.
